Integer division is legal and compiles.

items.stem: Two object references a and b refer to the same object. After b.setX(9), calling a.getX() returns 9 because:

options.text: a and b are aliases to one object
options.rationale: Correct: assigning a reference copies the reference, not the object, so both point to the same instance.

options.text: a copied the object's fields when assigned
options.rationale: Reference assignment does not copy the object.
getX returns the current field value, which was changed.

options.text: Java passes objects by value of the object
options.rationale: Java copies the reference value, so both still share one object.

items.explanation: Correct: assigning a reference copies the reference, not the object, so both point to the same instance.
